# Doc surfaces map

Which file covers what, and the kind of change that means it needs a look. Not every commit touches every row — most touch one or two.

| Surface | Covers | Update when... |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | Source of truth: golden rules, project layout table, the "adding a new page object" / "adding a new component fixture" rituals. `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (and any other tool-specific pointer file) points here rather than repeating it in full. | A new file/dir is added under the tracked paths; a new convention, alias, or rule of thumb is introduced; a ritual's steps change. |
| `README.md` (git-tracked as `README.me` — this repo's filesystem is case-insensitive, so both names resolve to the same file; edit either, git only sees `README.me`) | Human-facing project tour: what the project is, first-time setup, the project-structure tree, the onboarding-from-boilerplate framing. | Same file/dir additions as AGENTS.md's layout table — keep the two trees consistent with each other, not just with reality. Setup/tooling changes (new script, new env var) also land here. |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | A condensed, "highest-priority rules repeated for quick reference" subset of AGENTS.md's golden rules, for Copilot Chat. | A _must-follow_ rule (not just any golden rule) is added, changed, or removed in AGENTS.md. Match its existing altitude — it's deliberately shorter than AGENTS.md, don't pad it out to match one-for-one. |
| `.github/prompts/new-page-object.prompt.md` | The 4-step "add a new page object" ritual, as a Copilot Chat slash-prompt. | The page-object-adding ritual in AGENTS.md changes (new step, reordered step, a file that must be touched changes name/location). |
| `.github/prompts/explain-repo.prompt.md` | A repo-orientation prompt for Copilot Chat. | The overall architecture description changes significantly (new top-level concept, not just a new file in an existing category). |
| `.github/prompts/onboard-client-project.prompt.md` + `.github/prompts/onboard-client-project.references.md` | The onboarding wizard that converts this boilerplate into a real client project, and its file-by-file placeholder map. Unique to this repo (survey-playwright and other already-onboarded client repos don't carry this). | A new placeholder/token is introduced (a new `your-url-here`-style value, a new env key, a new file that a real project must customize); an existing placeholder's location or shape changes; a file the wizard reads/deletes is renamed or removed. |
| `.github/agents/flaky-test-investigator.agent.md` | A Copilot agent definition for investigating flaky/failing tests — loads `AGENTS.md`, `playwright.config.ts`, `config/projects.ts`, `testFixtures/base.ts` as its own context. | The auto-fixtures it name-checks (`blockAnalytics`, `cookieConsent`) change name/behavior; the files it's told to load as context are renamed/moved; the flakiness classification categories stop matching how this suite actually fails. |
| `.github/skills/write-test/` (POM-then-spec authoring conventions) | Locator priority, POM class shape, spec `describe` structure, tagging rules, the registration ritual, plus `references/this-repo.md`'s cached discovery of this repo's actual layout/aliases/lint rules. | A testing convention changes: locator priority, POM class shape, spec structure, tagging rules, the registration ritual. Also update `references/this-repo.md` specifically whenever the cached layout/alias/lint-rule facts it lists go stale (e.g. a new environment file is added, the first content-block component ships, a new lint rule lands in `eslint.config.mjs`). |
| `.github/skills/code-review/` | Convention-review checklist and severity/coverage rubric for reviewing specs, page objects, components, and fixtures against this repo's Playwright rules. | Review standards change (new must-follow convention, changed locator priority, new fixture pattern, new tagging/device-scope rule), or checklist guidance becomes stale/overly specific to files/examples that no longer exist. |
| `.github/skills/register-pom/` | Fixture-registration steps (`types/types.ts`'s `Pages`/`Components`, `testFixtures/base.ts`, `BasePage`). | The registration mechanism itself changes (new fixture factory, new registry file, changed constructor wiring, a type/file renamed by a casing-convention change). |
| `.github/skills/using-utils/` | Lookup table for every file in `utils/` — fixture-wired vs. direct-import, one-liner per helper, guidance on wiring a new one in. Points at README.md's "Quality & Accessibility Helpers" section for the full prose/examples rather than duplicating them. | A file is added/removed under `utils/`; an existing helper moves from direct-import to fixture-wired (or vice versa); README's "Quality & Accessibility Helpers" section gains/loses a subsection. |
| `.github/skills/doc-sync/` (this skill) | This file, the SKILL.md workflow, and any eval suite under `evals/`. | The doc-surfaces map itself goes stale (a new surface appears, an old one is removed/renamed) — which is exactly the kind of drift this skill exists to catch, so hold it to the same standard. |
| `.vscode/playwright.code-snippets` | IDE snippets that encode current import/convention patterns (aliases, fixture usage shape, POM/component scaffolds). | An alias changes, or the shape of a commonly-snippeted pattern (e.g. a new page-object constructor signature) changes. Lower priority than the above — only touch it if a snippet would now produce something that fails lint/typecheck. |
| eslint `jsdoc/*` rules (`eslint.config.mjs`) | Not a doc file, but the mechanism that says every method needs a JSDoc block, a description, a `@returns`, and correctly-named `@param`s. | Any method eslint flags under `jsdoc/require-jsdoc`, `jsdoc/require-description`, `jsdoc/require-returns`, or `jsdoc/check-param-names` in the files you're reviewing. |
| eslint `@typescript-eslint/naming-convention` + `check-file/filename-naming-convention` rules (`eslint.config.mjs`) | Not a doc file, but the mechanism enforcing PascalCase types/POM filenames and camelCase everything else. | A new type/interface/class or file is added that these rules would flag — fix the code rather than the docs in this case, but if the _rule itself_ changes (a new selector, a relaxed exemption), that's worth a line in `write-test/references/this-repo.md`'s lint-rules section. |

## What usually does _not_ need a doc update

Most `tests/**/*.spec.ts` changes are additive test coverage, not a new convention — they don't need README/AGENTS changes unless they introduce a pattern worth documenting for the next person writing a similar test (a new tag, a new assertion helper shape). Bug fixes inside an existing method's body, with no signature or behavior-contract change, usually don't need a JSDoc rewrite either — only add/edit JSDoc where eslint actually flags it or where the fix changed what the method returns/accepts.
